selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What are the two main ideas named in this passage?
questions.answer: They are createdness and contingency.

questions.question: Which groups of Muslim thinkers are said to have shown these two ideas with many proofs?
questions.answer: Scholars of Islamic belief and theology, and also wise Muslim thinkers, are mentioned.

questions.question: What do those thinkers notice in the world that helps their argument?
questions.answer: They notice that things in the world keep changing.

questions.question: If things keep changing, what does the passage say about the world?
questions.answer: It says the world does not last forever in the same state and was brought into existence.

questions.question: If the world was brought into existence, what must also be true?
questions.answer: There must be a Creator who made it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about something whose own nature does not make its existence necessary?
questions.answer: It is not eternal or necessary by itself.

questions.question: If a thing could either exist or not exist, what does that show?
questions.answer: It shows that the thing depends on another cause and is not self-existing.

questions.question: Which idea in the passage is more about something not having to exist by itself?
questions.answer: Contingency is the idea about that.

questions.question: What is the “First Truth” about in this passage?
questions.answer: It is about createdness and contingency.

questions.question: Are these ideas presented as weak guesses or as strongly supported teachings?
questions.answer: They are presented as strongly supported by many proofs.

questions.question: What part of the world do the scholars use as evidence first?
questions.answer: They use the fact that the world and its things change.

questions.question: According to the passage, can the world be without a beginning if it is changing?
questions.answer: No, it is described as brought into existence.

questions.question: Once the world is understood as brought into existence, what follows next?
questions.answer: A Maker is needed to bring it into existence.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a thing whose own being does not explain why it exists?
questions.answer: It says that such a thing is not necessary by itself.

questions.question: What two possibilities are mentioned for that kind of thing?
questions.answer: It could exist, or it could fail to exist.

questions.question: If both possibilities are open, what does that tell us about the thing?
questions.answer: It tells us that it is dependent and not everlasting by itself.

questions.question: What truth does this passage begin to explain?
questions.answer: It begins to explain the first truth.

questions.question: What two topics are included in that truth?
questions.answer: It includes createdness and contingency.

questions.question: Who is said to have proven these topics with many evidences?
questions.answer: Muslim scholars of belief and theology, along with sages of Islam, are said to have done that.

questions.question: What everyday fact about the world is the starting point of their reasoning?
questions.answer: The starting point is that things in the world change.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude from the world’s changing condition?
questions.answer: It concludes that the world is temporary and created.

questions.question: What does the passage say must exist if something created the world?
questions.answer: A Maker must exist.

questions.question: What does “not necessary” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means a thing does not have existence by its own nature.

questions.question: Why is a thing not eternal if its existence and non-existence are both possible?
questions.answer: Because it does not have to exist on its own and could just as well not exist.
